extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in multiple stages. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to identify and eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format and undertaking necessary corrections. In the third stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark. This process resulted in 11.5K questions from an initial collection of 13K questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected and annotated by over 50 university students specializing in the relevant subjects. Annotators followed a comprehensive protocol that included: collecting questions with one or more images, ensuring college-level difficulty, categorizing questions as multiple-choice or open-ended, annotating all fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). All questions were written in English and should not be ambiguous. The annotation protocol is detailed in Appendix A.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples from the dataset were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for detailed review and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into a few-shot development set (5 questions per subject), a validation set (approximately 900 questions), and a test set (10.5K questions). Version changes are documented in the paper (e.g., v1 to v4 with updates to model results, author contributions, and error corrections).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and to monitor progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark aims to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI but should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system to demonstrate broad and deep subject knowledge as well as expert-level understanding and reasoning capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. MMMU combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, but this may not capture all aspects of expert-level reasoning. The benchmark is challenging even for advanced models like GPT-4V (55.7% accuracy), indicating substantial room for improvement. Error analysis on GPT-4V reveals that 35% of errors are perceptual, 29% stem from lack of knowledge, and 26% are due to flaws in reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating large multimodal models on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks. Use cases include: Testing, Validation, and benchmarking of multimodal foundation models. The benchmark is intended to assess models' capabilities in perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse professional domains at the college level.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For multiple-choice questions: one correct answer from multiple options. For open-ended questions: one correct short answer. Explanations are provided for 17.62% of questions (2,035 out of 11,550).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects covered by the benchmark. Annotators were selected to represent expertise across Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering disciplines.
